newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures erode late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures erode late, end mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures eroded late and ended pit trading barely mixed.
Traders said quiet afternoon range-trading turned lively during the final half-hour as dealers and locals sold enough to uncover sell stops in December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500s.
The premium over cash also shrank toward 4.00 points, narrow enough to attract arbitrage sell programs.
"We got sell stops and a real good round of sell programs," said a floor analyst in S&P 500 futures. "Maybe we got a little too far ahead of ourselves on window-dressing this morning."
Fair value on Monday stood at about a 5.40-point premium. Arbitrage buy programs were expected at roughly a 6.10-point premium. Sell programs needed 4.75 points over cash or less.
Futures had bounced up early and later ignored a selloff in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which broke down after some stronger than expected U.S. economic data.
August U.S. new home sales rose 4.7 percent to an 832,000 unit annual rate, well above forecasts for a 39,000 decline to a 744,000-unit rate. July's figures were revised upward.
The September Chicago purchasing managers index slipped to 56.3 from 60.0, near forecasts for 56.0.
News that August U.S. personal income and spending rose 0.6 percent, close to forecasts, had limited impact.
Futures had spent much of the late morning and afternoon languishing inside tight intraday ranges until the late selloff that spilled over from the high-technology stocks.
During the morning's rally, December S&P 500s hurdled key resistance near the 692.00-35 area and looked ripe for a challenge of the contract high at 697.50, before it stalled.

Dec S&P 500s settled unchanged at 691.40, Value Lines fell 1.95 to 642.00, Nikkei rose 65.0 to 21,575.0, Midcap eased 0.80 to 243.95, and NYSE Composite rose 0.05 to 368.90. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
